28.0.0.en: Gibeon: a city inhabited by priests, lying about 5 miles northwest of Jerusalem.

28.0.1.en: In the fourth year of King Zedekiah, at the beginning of his reign (he means the first half of his reign, since he reigned eleven years, and the fourth year corresponds to 593 BC), one of the false prophets came forward, called Hananiah the son of Azur, from the city of Gibeon, which is inhabited by priests, so he is thought to have been a priest. Because Gibeon is a city in the tribe of Benjamin and near Jerusalem, Hananiah came to Jerusalem and stood in the house of the Lord, where many gather, to declare his false prophecy. This was in the presence of Jeremiah, to make the people doubt the prophecies of Jeremiah.

28.1.0.en: Note the power of deception in Hananiah's prophecy, which relies on:

28.1.2.en: 2- He speaks in the house of the Lord before the crowds with boldness.

28.1.3.en: 3- He speaks in the presence of Jeremiah, declaring the error and mistake of his prophecies.

28.1.4.en: 4- He uses the same expressions that Jeremiah uses: "Thus speaketh the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel... I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon...", using the same visual aid that Jeremiah used.

28.1.5.en: 5- He fixes a time for the fulfillment of his prophecy, namely after two years.

28.1.6.en: Be careful before strange, misleading teachings, for they have a logical form and a dazzling appearance; but as long as they conflict with the teachings of the Church and the holy Fathers, they are misleading. Do not rush after them, but lift up your heart in prayer and hold fast to what you have, that is, what you learned from the Church, lest you go astray.

28.2.0.en: The summary of the prophecy is the end of Nebuchadnezzar's enslavement of all the lands he occupied, including the kingdom of Judah, after two years' time, the breaking of Babylon, and the return of the vessels of the house of the Lord which Nebuchadnezzar had seized from the temple in Jerusalem. Note his preoccupation with material things, namely the vessels of the house of the Lord, before the captives, who are more important. Of course his prophecy is false, because Jeremiah declared that the Babylonian captivity would continue for 70 years (Jer 25:12).

28.3.0.en: He gives a second proof of the end of Babylon's enslavement of the kingdom of Judah, that is, the breaking of its yoke: the return of King Jeconiah king of Judah, who was carried captive to Babylon, and all the captives with him, to Jerusalem and Judea.

28.4.0.en: Jeremiah was not troubled by the deceit of the false Hananiah. He stood before him in the house of the Lord and answered him calmly and with power.

28.5.0.en: Jeremiah declared his agreement, not with Hananiah's prophecy, but with the return of the captives and of the vessels of the house of the Lord. This will indeed happen, but after 70 years; it is the wish of the whole kingdom of Judah, but it will not be after two years as Hananiah said.

28.6.0.en: Jeremiah qualified his words to Hananiah: although he agrees with this wish, he shows his lying in what follows in the next two verses.

28.7.0.en: Jeremiah said to Hananiah that any prophet is known to be truthful by the fulfillment of his prophecy in its time. So it was with the ancient prophets who preceded him: if his word is true, what he says will come to pass. The truth is that Hananiah's word conflicts not only with Jeremiah's word but with many earlier prophets such as Joel, Amos, Hosea, Micah, Zephaniah, Nahum, Habakkuk and others.

28.7.1.en: Do not be troubled by the error of false teachers, and be sure that your God is with you, supporting you, and will fulfill what you believe. Satan is not only a liar and the father of lies, but he speaks with boldness and impudence, so pay no attention to his words.

28.8.s.en: (3) The breaking of the wooden yoke

28.8.0.en: Hananiah supported his words with a visual aid: he took the yoke which Jeremiah wore on his neck and broke it before the assembled people to prove his prophecy that the bondage of Babylon would end, using the moving visual aid to mislead the people.

28.9.0.en: Hananiah affirmed that Babylon's enslavement of the kingdom of Judah and all the lands around it would end after two years. When Jeremiah saw his insistence on error, he left him and went his way: the servant does his duty and is not troubled by the abundance of evil, even if the wicked persist in it.

28.9.1.en: Do not deceive others by letting them hear what they want to hear, even if it is against the truth, and do not believe what you wish, lest others lead you astray and you drift from the truth. Rather, seek God and accept His word, so that you repent of your sins and are ready at all times.

28.10.0.en: Jeremiah did not rush to utter words to rebuke Hananiah but turned to God and prayed until it was revealed to him what to say to Hananiah, for he speaks with the voice of God and not with his own personal words.

28.10.1.en: Make sure that what you say is the voice of God. Do not be hasty in answering, and seek God to guide you, however much others provoke and threaten you, and be reassured, for God will teach you the truth and keep you from the evil of enemies.

28.11.0.en: Jeremiah declared the word of God to Hananiah: that in haste and deceit he broke the wooden yoke to proclaim falsely that the bondage of Babylon would end, but the truth is that this word is a deception of the people, and God will allow yokes of iron in place of the wooden yokes; that is, the bondage of Babylon will be harsh and cannot be escaped except after the fullness of time, that is, after seventy years.

28.12.0.en: God will allow Babylon to enslave all the peoples, and likewise all its possessions, like the animals.

28.13.0.en: Jeremiah declared the word of God clearly in a specific rebuke of Hananiah the false prophet, for Jeremiah said to him: you are not a prophet from God, but you came of yourself and falsely claimed that your words are from God.

28.14.0.en: The second divine declaration to Hananiah is his punishment for his false prophecy: he will be cast off, not from his country as the Babylonians will do to the inhabitants of the kingdom of Judah, but from the face of the whole earth, that is, he will die as the recompense for his lying, as happened with Ananias and Sapphira, who lied and died at once (Acts 5:1-11).

28.15.0.en: God's word was indeed fulfilled: Hananiah died in the same year, two months after his false prophecy, which was in the fifth month of the fourth year of King Zedekiah; Hananiah died in the seventh month. Here we see the mercy of God, who gave him two months as an opportunity to repent, and that is better than the case of Ananias and Sapphira, who died at once. He prophesied that after two years the bondage would end, but only two months passed and he died, while the Babylonian bondage lasted seventy years.

28.15.1.en: God gives you the opportunity of this life for repentance and returning to Him, so do not be negligent and neglect it, and accept rebuke from others, for it may be a divine message to you.

29.0.0.en: After Nebuchadnezzar carried captive Jeconiah the king, who is also called Jehoiachin, and with him the great men who were in Jerusalem, Jeremiah sent this letter, and this was in 597 BC. Jeremiah sent this letter from Jerusalem to the leaders of the captives, the priests and the prophets, to read it to all the people.

29.1.0.en: With Jeconiah the captive king were his wife the queen and also some men whom the king of Babylon had made eunuchs to work for him, especially in the palaces of his wives, in addition to the Jews distinguished in the various trades.

29.2.0.en: King Zedekiah king of Judah sent two of his officials, Elasah and Gemariah, to establish a good relationship with Nebuchadnezzar, who had heard of the attempt to form an alliance against him in the west of his kingdom, among whom was the king of Judah. So Jeremiah sent his letter with these two messengers, who were friends of his.

29.3.0.en: The speaker is the God of Israel, that is, the God of the people captive in humiliation and bondage. He declares His fatherhood and care for them to reassure them, and confirms this reassurance by describing Himself as the Lord of hosts, that is, the Mighty One, able to do all things.

29.3.1.en: If affliction passes through your life, be sure that your God, who always loves you, will not forget you. He is the Mighty One, able to rescue you when you return to Him in repentance, and He fixes the right time to lift all your troubles from you; and also during the affliction He will not leave you but will comfort your heart as long as you hold fast to Him.

29.4.0.en: God commands them to settle in Babylon and not be deceived by the errors of the false prophets, who make them imagine that the return from Babylon will be after two years. He confirms this settling through two things:

29.4.1.en: 1- Building private houses for themselves in which to dwell.

29.4.2.en: 2- Planting gardens of fruit trees to eat their fruit, which will ripen after years. This means that He calls them to accept divine discipline, which helps them to repent, and afterward God will return them to Jerusalem, after seventy years, so that their repentance may be complete.

29.5.0.en: He confirms their settling by a third thing, which is calling the young people to marry, establish new families and bear children. There is no need to postpone marriage, since they have seventy years ahead of them in captivity. Of course the marriage will be to believing Jews and not to pagans.

29.6.0.en: He also confirms their settling by a fourth thing, which is that they pray for the kingdom of Babylon, so that when it has peace they enjoy peace and settled life. This is what the Church does in praying for the city in which she is established and for the civil rulers, in the prayers of the Liturgy and the various ritual prayers (the Litany of Peace, the Litany for the Ruler)...

29.7.0.en: God warns them against listening to the lies of the prophets, diviners and dreamers, for it is their words of deception and not the word of God; Babylon will not be destroyed after two years as they claim.

29.8.0.en: If God has allowed His people to be disciplined so that they repent, it is for a fixed period, seventy years in captivity, and after that He returns them to their land to enjoy their worship of Him.

29.8.1.en: God's plan is the salvation of His children, and afflictions are one link in the links of this plan, so that they may be with Him in heaven.

29.9.0.en: I will be found of you: you will feel My presence in your midst.

29.9.1.en: God encourages His children that when their repentance is complete and they pray to Him, not only with their lips but with their faith and all their feelings, God hears them and makes them feel His presence in their midst, and brings them back from captivity to their land.

29.10.0.en: God rebukes His people captive in Babylon for describing the two false prophets, Ahab the son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, mentioned in (v. 21), as prophets from God, and consequently believing their lies that Babylon would be overturned after two years, which hindered them from repentance and returning to God.

29.11.0.en: Then God speaks to the captives about their brothers who are still in Jerusalem and with whom King Zedekiah dwells; that is, He gives the captives a message from God about those who remain in Jerusalem.

29.12.0.en: Those who remained in Jerusalem thought that they were righteous and those in captivity wicked, so God declared to those remaining in Jerusalem that His wrath would come upon them, to die in three ways:

29.12.2.en: 2- Death by disease, that is, by pestilence.

29.12.4.en: Their state will be very wretched and no one will accept dealing with them, like the bad winter fig which could not be eaten, explained earlier in (ch. 24).

29.13.0.en: To be removed: a cause of trouble.

29.13.1.en: A curse: the alliance of the nations against them.

29.13.2.en: An astonishment: the nations marvel at their humiliation and their God's abandonment of them.

29.13.3.en: An hissing: they hiss at them in mockery.

29.13.4.en: A reproach: an example of humiliation and ridicule.

29.13.5.en: God completes His punishment of those remaining in Jerusalem and Judea by the continuance of His wrath upon them: they die by the sword, famine and pestilence even after the Babylonians drive them out and transfer them from their land to other lands, and they become a cause of trouble in the lands to which they go; everyone mocks them and marvels at the humiliation into which they have fallen.

29.14.0.en: He continues his words to those remaining in Jerusalem, rebuking them for not obeying His prophets whom He sent early, that is, for many years up to now, to call them to faith and repentance; because of this disobedience the wrath of God came upon them.

29.15.0.en: He returns to direct his words to the captives in Babylon and gives them a new message, making clear in his words that it is He who sent them to Babylon, that is, He allowed this discipline so that they might accept it, submit to God and repent.

29.16.0.en: Jeremiah prophesies about the two false prophets whom the captives thought to be prophets from God, declaring that the king of Babylon will kill them, and that is a divine punishment because of the multitude of their sins, especially their leading the people astray.

29.17.0.en: The king of Babylon will kill them, not with the sword, but he will torture them by burning them with fire or boiling oil, so that they die a horrible death which becomes an example of shame and cursing. God allows this so that the people may fear and keep away from error.

29.18.0.en: God adds another reason, beside the lies and the leading of the people astray by these two prophets: that they committed adultery with their neighbors' wives, which is the sin of adultery and betrayal.

29.19.0.en: God asked Jeremiah to speak to one of the false prophets in Babylon, who was called Shemaiah the Nehelamite. The details of this letter are not given, but in essence it is a rebuke of Shemaiah for the letter he sent to Zephaniah the priest to stir people up against the word of God through the mouth of Jeremiah.

29.20.0.en: Jeremiah's letter to Shemaiah shows the following:

29.20.1.en: 1- The speaker, the author of the letter, is God, the Lord of hosts, that is, the Mighty One, that Shemaiah may fear and repent of his evil.

29.20.2.en: 2- Zephaniah had a distinguished position among the priests in Jerusalem, so Shemaiah sent his letter to him.

29.20.3.en: 3- Shemaiah wanted to stir up all the priests against Jeremiah, so he directed his letter not only to Zephaniah but to all the priests; but he sent it to Zephaniah because he was foremost among them and their chief, and he attached to it letters with the same words to the priests.

29.20.4.en: 4- The Lord of hosts is the God of Israel, that is, the One who shepherds him, and the letters of false prophets such as Shemaiah cannot change His plan: He disciplines them so that they repent and then brings them back from captivity.

29.20.5.en: 5- These letters are in the name of Shemaiah and not in the name of God, so they are his own words and not, as Shemaiah claims, from God.

29.21.0.en: The stocks: a piece of wood with a place to fasten the hands and feet, where the person is laid on his back and his hand and foot are bound in it so that he cannot move inside the prison.

29.21.1.en: Shemaiah's letter to Zephaniah contains the following:

29.21.2.en: 1- Shemaiah's claim that God made him chief priest, and not Jehoiada, about whom we know nothing, though he is thought to have been a high official among the priests and known to all; he died, and Shemaiah set himself up in his place and claimed that God had appointed him.

29.21.3.en: 2- He describes Jeremiah the prophet as mad, and therefore his words are unsound and are not the word of God.

29.21.4.en: 3- He claimed that God gave him the right to arrest the wicked who speak against the temple, like Jeremiah.

29.21.5.en: 4- He calls the priests to seize Jeremiah, bind him in the stocks and put him in prison. From this it is understood that this Jehoiada was the chief of the guard responsible for protecting the temple and that Shemaiah took his place, so he commands the priests and their assistants to seize Jeremiah and throw him into prison.

29.21.6.en: All this, of course, is lies and claims of Shemaiah, and God is utterly innocent of them.

29.22.0.en: Shemaiah says in his letter to Zephaniah, reproaching him for his failure to rebuke Jeremiah, who is from the village of Anathoth near Jerusalem.

29.23.0.en: It is long: the stay in Babylon will be for a long time.

29.23.1.en: Shemaiah's letter to Zephaniah makes clear that Jeremiah erred because he sent a letter to Babylon asking the Jews to settle in it, build houses, plant fruit gardens and wait to eat from them. In Shemaiah's opinion this is against the people of God and an alliance with the Babylonian enemies.

29.23.2.en: But the truth is the word of Jeremiah and the word of God to discipline His people by staying in captivity for 70 years so that they repent.

29.24.0.en: When Shemaiah's letter reached Zephaniah the priest, he made it known not only to all the priests and those working in the temple, but also declared it to Jeremiah so that he would stop his prophecy, for it was a kind of threat to him. But Jeremiah did not fear, and God revealed to him to send a letter to him rebuking him for his letters and his lies, so he sent him a letter as we have mentioned.

29.24.1.en: Do not fear the threats of the wicked, for they have no authority over you; God alone has authority, and He protects you. So continue to hold fast to His commandments and to proclaim the truth, and do not fear anyone.

29.25.s.en: (3) A second letter to the captives

29.25.0.en: God commanded Jeremiah to send a second letter to the captives in Babylon in which He declares His punishment of Shemaiah, who led the captives astray and also those in Jerusalem. What is meant by declaring God's punishment is that the Jews should keep away from these errors and repent, so that God may forgive them.

29.26.0.en: The divine punishment of Shemaiah is that he will have no offspring living to see the return from captivity after 70 years; that is, his sons, his daughters and his offspring die and leave no offspring after him, so his offspring will not enjoy God's blessing for His people returning from captivity.

29.26.1.en: God had already declared His punishment through Jeremiah on another false prophet, Hananiah (ch. 28:15-16), by his death, and he died quickly. The divine purpose is also that the lies of the false prophets not be listened to.

29.26.2.en: Keep away from any strange teachings you hear outside the Church that conflict with her teachings, and consult your father of confession about these gatherings, so that you do not expose yourself to thoughts that draw you away from God, however beautiful and attractive their form, because the devil is a deceiver who can take the form of an angel to lead the children of God astray.
